findings.title: Sender check is skipped entirely when no Integration row exists yet
findings.body: In GitHubInstallation.dispatch, when Integration.objects.get(external_id=installation_id) raises DoesNotExist, the code returns pipeline.next_step() immediately. The new check that the OAuth-authenticated GitHub user matches integration.metadata['sender']['login'] is only reached when an Integration row already exists. So the user-mismatch protection that this PR advertises is not applied on that path, and the pipeline proceeds to build_integration without any verification that the authenticated user installed the app. The check should be enforced regardless of whether the Integration row exists, or the flow should explicitly require the sender to be known before continuing.

findings.title: KeyError when an existing Integration has no 'sender' in metadata
findings.body: integration.metadata['sender']['login'] is accessed directly. build_integration only stores 'sender' when state.get('sender') is truthy, and integrations created before this metadata existed, or created without it, will not have the key. The result is an unhandled KeyError (HTTP 500) in the installation pipeline instead of the intended error page. Use a safe lookup and fail with error() when the sender is missing.

findings.title: OAuth authorize redirect builds URL without encoding parameters
findings.body: The authorize redirect concatenates state and redirect_uri into the query string without URL-encoding them (f"...&state={state}&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"). redirect_uri is an absolute URL containing ':' and '/' and any '&' or '#' in it would break the query. Use urllib.parse.urlencode for the parameters.

findings.title: Missing code parameter is sent to GitHub without validation
findings.body: data['code'] is taken from request.GET.get('code') and may be None. The request is still sent to the access-token endpoint, and the failure is only detected afterwards via a missing access_token. Validate that code is present before calling GitHub, and handle a failed safe_urlopen (network error) explicitly, since it is not wrapped in any error handling.

findings.title: Tests do not cover the state mismatch or code reuse failure paths
findings.body: The new failure modes listed in the PR (state signature mismatch, GitHub rejecting the code/access token) have no dedicated tests. The only negative test added is user mismatch, and the bypass path where no Integration row exists is not tested. Also the assertion uses responses.calls[2] by index, which is brittle against changes in the number of mocked calls.
